stories.title: From the Pine Corridor to Tokyo
stories.blurb: How the shogun's city kept order for a century and a half, and how ships at Uraga and swords at Sakurada Gate brought it down.

steps.name: The sword in the Pine Corridor
steps.what: Asano wounded Kira inside the castle and was ordered to commit seppuku that day.
steps.why: Drawing a sword in the castle broke the core rule of shogunal order.

steps.name: The rōnin's vendetta
steps.what: The Akō rōnin killed Kira and were later ordered to commit seppuku.
steps.why: The case set loyalty against law and became Japan's favorite story.

steps.name: Yoshimune's reforms
steps.what: The eighth shogun launched the Kyōhō reforms.
steps.why: Debt and debased coin threatened the shogunate.

steps.name: A box for petitions
steps.what: Commoners could now drop signed petitions to the shogun.
steps.why: One petition produced a free hospital for the poor.

steps.name: Tanuma's commercial state
steps.what: Tanuma taxed guilds and drained marshes.
steps.why: Famine and riots ended his era in disgrace.

steps.name: Riots and the Kansei reforms
steps.what: Edo crowds sacked rice shops; Sadanobu took power and imposed austerity.
steps.why: The city's hunger could now unseat a government.

steps.name: The Tenpō reforms
steps.what: Mizuno banned luxury and moved the theatres.
steps.why: The last great attempt at restoration failed within two years.

steps.name: Black ships at Uraga
steps.what: Perry's squadron demanded a treaty.
steps.why: The shogunate could not defend Edo Bay.

steps.name: Convention of Kanagawa
steps.what: Japan opened two ports to American ships.
steps.why: It ended two centuries of seclusion.

steps.name: The Harris Treaty
steps.what: Trade treaty signed without imperial approval.
steps.why: It set off the Ansei purge and a wave of terror.
steps.wikipedia: Treaty of Amity and Commerce (United States–Japan)

steps.name: Sakuradamon incident
steps.what: Rōnin killed the tairō in the snow.
steps.why: Shogunal authority never recovered.

steps.name: Namamugi incident
steps.what: Satsuma retainers killed an English merchant on the Tōkaidō.
steps.why: It led to the bombardment of Kagoshima.

steps.name: Edo surrenders
steps.what: Edo Castle was handed over without battle.
steps.why: A city of a million was spared.

steps.name: Edo becomes Tokyo
steps.what: Edo was renamed and the emperor moved in.
steps.why: The shogun's city became the capital.

stories.title: Ash, Ink and Fire: Living in Edo
stories.blurb: The townspeople's Edo: fires and quakes, prints and novels, Dutch books and fireworks.

steps.name: Fuji's ash
steps.what: Ash from Fuji fell on Edo.
steps.why: Villages on Fuji's slope were ruined for years.

steps.name: Riot and fireworks
steps.what: After rice riots, fireworks honored the dead.
steps.why: Ryōgoku became Edo's summer playground.

steps.name: Brocade prints
steps.what: Full-color woodblock prints appeared.
steps.why: Cheap color images became an Edo specialty.

steps.name: Dissection at Kozukappara
steps.what: Physicians compared a body with a Dutch atlas.
steps.why: Observation beat inherited doctrine.

steps.name: The Meiwa fire
steps.what: A fire burned across the city.
steps.why: Fire shaped Edo's building and money.

steps.name: Kaitai Shinsho
steps.what: The translated anatomy appeared.
steps.why: It founded Dutch learning.

steps.name: Smashing the rice shops
steps.what: Crowds sacked rice dealers.
steps.why: Famine reached the city.

steps.name: Yaji and Kita take the road
steps.what: A comic road novel.
steps.why: Travel became a pastime for commoners.

steps.name: Yotsuya Kaidan
steps.what: A ghost play premiered.
steps.why: Kabuki turned to dark everyday life.

steps.name: The Great Wave
steps.what: Hokusai's landscape print.
steps.why: Landscapes became a mass genre.

steps.name: Hiroshige's Tōkaidō
steps.what: Fifty-three stations from Nihonbashi.
steps.why: The highway became art.
steps.wikipedia: The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō

steps.name: The Ansei earthquake
steps.what: A quake and fires killed thousands.
steps.why: Catfish prints showed public feeling.

steps.name: One Hundred Famous Views
steps.what: Hiroshige's farewell to Edo.
steps.why: It inspired Van Gogh.
steps.wikipedia: One Hundred Famous Views of Edo

steps.name: Yokohama opens
steps.what: A new trading port opened.
steps.why: Silk and tea went abroad; new ideas came in.
